summary: Khôra is a dice-driven engine-builder where you pick 2 of 7 actions each round and must adapt your plan to the die roll you get, climbing tracks that snowball into stronger resources, cards, and points. It plays fast for its depth, with tight turns and a real puzzle in reconciling your strategy with variable dice.
praised: Clever, tense action-selection puzzle balancing planned strategy against dice randomness
Multiple viable paths to victory (economy, military, culture, politics)
Fast turns and low downtime despite meaningful depth
Good component quality and iconography once learned
Strong replayability from varied strategies and achievement goals
criticised: Steep learning curve and dense rulebook/iconography for a first play
Dice manipulation mitigates but doesn't eliminate swingy bad rolls
Low direct player interaction can make it feel solitaire-ish
Some symbol/track overload makes teaching it to new players hard
End-of-game scoring can feel a bit fiddly to tally

interaction.kind: mostly parallel engine-building with light racing for shared resources/track positions

scoring.why: Points accumulate from multiple tracks, achievements, and end-game bonuses tied to how far you advanced across economy, culture, and military development
